questions.stem: Which city is the official seat of the European Parliament?
questions.explanation: The European Parliament's official seat is Strasbourg, in Alsace, though much of its work also takes place in Brussels. Luxembourg hosts the Parliament's administration, not its seat, and Geneva is outside the EU altogether.

questions.stem: In which year did France help found the European Economic Community with the Treaty of Rome?
questions.explanation: France was one of the six founding members in 1957, with West Germany, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg. 1992 is the Maastricht Treaty, and 2002 the arrival of euro notes and coins.

questions.stem: Why is 9 May « la Journée de l'Europe »?
options: The Berlin Wall fell on 9 May 1989, reuniting the two halves of Europe.
Robert Schuman proposed pooling coal and steel production on 9 May 1950.
The Treaty of Rome founding the European community was signed on 9 May 1957.
The euro notes and coins came into circulation on 9 May 2002.
questions.explanation: The French foreign minister's declaration of 9 May 1950 led to the European Coal and Steel Community, the first step towards the EU. The Treaty of Rome was signed in March 1957.

questions.stem: What does « l'espace Schengen » allow?
options: A single currency shared by member countries
Voting in any member country's national elections
Free university study in any member country
questions.explanation: The Schengen area removes routine passport checks at internal borders. The single currency is the euro, and its members are not the same set of countries.

questions.stem: What is « une terre d'accueil »?
options: A piece of farmland for sale
A refugee camp at a border
A country that people are leaving behind
questions.explanation: « L'accueil » is welcome, so « une terre d'accueil » is a land that takes in migrants. The country people leave is « le pays d'origine ».

questions.stem: What does « s'intégrer » mean when talking about migrants?
options: To become part of a new society
To return to one's home country
questions.explanation: « S'intégrer » is to settle into and take part in a new community, and « l'intégration » is the process. Returning home is « rentrer au pays ».

questions.stem: What is « la langue maternelle » of a person?
options: The language they speak most fluently now
The first language they learnt as a child
The language of their current country
questions.explanation: « La langue maternelle » is your first language, whoever you learnt it from and wherever you now live. A migrant may come to speak a second language more fluently, but it does not become their mother tongue.

questions.stem: « Le dépaysement » has no single English equivalent. What does it describe?
options: The feeling of being somewhere unfamiliar, far from home
The process of losing your citizenship by moving abroad
The loss of farmland as cities spread into the country
The paperwork needed to move to a new country
questions.explanation: « Dépaysé » means taken out of your own « pays ». The feeling can be disorienting or refreshing, as in a change of scenery. It is a mood, not a legal or administrative process.

questions.stem: What is « le bénévolat »?
questions.explanation: « Le bénévolat » is unpaid voluntary work, and a volunteer is « un(e) bénévole ». A donation is « un don ».

questions.stem: What is « une association caritative »?
questions.explanation: « Caritatif » comes from the Latin for charity, and it describes organisations that help people in need. A trade union is « un syndicat ».

questions.stem: What does « SDF » stand for, and what does it mean?
questions.explanation: « Sans domicile fixe » means having no fixed address, and « un SDF » is a homeless person. « Les sans-abri » is another common term.

questions.stem: What is « Les Restos du cœur »?
options: A charity that gives free meals to people in need
A chain of restaurants serving heart-healthy food
A guide that awards stars to restaurants
questions.explanation: The comedian Coluche founded Les Restos du cœur in 1985 to hand out free meals, and volunteers run it. Restaurant stars come from guides such as the Michelin guide.

questions.stem: What is Médecins sans frontières?
options: A medical aid organisation founded in France
A French law on doctors who work abroad in crises
A university medical course taught online
questions.explanation: Médecins sans frontières was founded in Paris in 1971 and gives emergency medical care in crises around the world. Its name means 'doctors without borders'.

questions.stem: « Dans un monde idéal, personne ne souffrirait de la faim. » What is the writer doing?
options: Imagining a better world using the conditional
Describing the present state of the world
Predicting what will happen in the future
Recounting what used to happen in the past
questions.explanation: « Souffrirait » is the conditional, the mood for hypothetical worlds: 'nobody would go hungry'. A prediction would use the future, « souffrira ».

questions.stem: What are « les inégalités sociales »?
options: Rules that apply to everyone equally
questions.explanation: « Les inégalités » are inequalities, a central idea in the subtopic of social justice. Rules that apply to everyone are a matter of « égalité ».

questions.stem: What is « l'empreinte carbone »?
questions.explanation: « Une empreinte » is a footprint or print, as in « empreintes digitales », fingerprints. A carbon tax is « la taxe carbone ».

questions.stem: What is « le gaspillage alimentaire »?
questions.explanation: « Gaspiller » means 'to waste', so « le gaspillage alimentaire » is food thrown away uneaten. A shortage is « une pénurie ».

questions.stem: What does « faire le tri sélectif » mean?
options: To choose the best students for a class
questions.explanation: « Le tri » is sorting, and « le tri sélectif » is separating household waste into bins for recycling. It is everyday vocabulary for the effects of humans on nature.

questions.stem: What is « le développement durable »?
options: Lasting economic growth at any cost
questions.explanation: « Durable » means lasting, and « le développement durable » meets present needs without harming those of future generations. Growth 'at any cost' is the opposite of the idea.

questions.stem: What are « les espèces menacées »?
questions.explanation: « Menacé » means 'threatened', so these species are at risk of dying out. Extinct species are « les espèces disparues », and invasive ones « les espèces envahissantes ».

questions.stem: « Si chacun réduisait sa consommation d'énergie, on émettrait moins de gaz à effet de serre. » What is claimed?
options: Less energy use would cut emissions.
Energy use is already falling every year.
Greenhouse gases come mostly from households.
Each person must use less energy by law.
questions.explanation: Si + imperfect with the conditional sets out a hypothesis: if everyone cut their use, emissions would fall. Nothing says use is already falling or that a law requires it.

questions.stem: What is « un internaute »?
questions.explanation: « Internaute » blends « internet » and « -naute », as in « astronaute ». A web designer is « un concepteur de sites web ».

questions.stem: What is « une infox »?
questions.explanation: « Infox » blends « information » and « intox », short for « intoxication », meaning disinformation. It was recommended in France as an alternative to « fake news ».

questions.stem: « Le Monde est un quotidien. » What is « un quotidien »?
questions.explanation: « Quotidien » means daily, so « un quotidien » is a paper published every day. A weekly is « un hebdomadaire ».

questions.stem: What is « le JT » on French television?
questions.explanation: « Le JT » is « le journal télévisé », the evening news bulletin. A weather report is « la météo ».

questions.stem: What is « la publicité mensongère »?
questions.explanation: « Mensonger » means deceptive, from « le mensonge », a lie. « La publicité » is advertising, not publicity in the English sense.

questions.stem: What does « Elle est accro aux écrans » mean?
options: She is close to the screen.
questions.explanation: « Accro », short for « accroché », is informal for 'addicted' or 'hooked'. « La dépendance aux écrans » is the more formal term for screen addiction.

questions.stem: In France, what is « le droit à la déconnexion »?
options: Households' right to cancel an internet contract at any time
Employees' right not to answer work messages outside working hours
Citizens' right to have their personal data deleted from websites
Students' right to keep their phones switched on during class
questions.explanation: French labour law requires larger employers to set rules so that staff can switch off after hours. Having your data deleted is a different right, « le droit à l'oubli ».

questions.stem: What are « les données personnelles »?
questions.explanation: « Les données » are data, and protecting personal data is a key issue for social media and privacy. A gift is « un don » or « un cadeau ».

questions.stem: « Les réseaux sociaux rapprochent ceux qui sont loin, mais éloignent ceux qui sont proches. » What is the writer's view?
options: They help both distant and nearby people equally.
They are mainly used by people who live far apart.
They should be banned for people living together.
They connect distant people but divide those nearby.
questions.explanation: « Rapprocher » is to bring closer and « éloigner » to push apart, so the sentence is built on a contrast. The writer sees a cost as well as a benefit, but proposes no ban.

questions.stem: In a text message, what does « mdr » mean?
questions.explanation: « Mdr » is « mort de rire », literally 'dead from laughing', the French equivalent of LOL. 'See you soon' is « a+ » or « à plus ».

questions.stem: In a text, what do « stp » and « bcp » stand for?
questions.explanation: Text messages drop vowels and keep key consonants: « stp » is « s'il te plaît », « bcp » is « beaucoup ». Such abbreviations are fine in a text to a friend but never in formal writing.

questions.stem: In relaxed speech, « je ne sais pas » often becomes « sais pas ». Which part is usually dropped first?
questions.explanation: Informal spoken French drops « ne » first, so « je sais pas » is the everyday form. « Pas » carries the negative meaning in speech, so it stays. In writing, keep « ne ».

questions.stem: Which French scientist won Nobel Prizes in both physics and chemistry?
questions.explanation: Marie Curie shared the 1903 physics prize and won the 1911 chemistry prize for her work on radioactivity, polonium and radium. Pasteur's fame rests on microbiology and vaccines.

questions.stem: What is Louis Pasteur known for?
options: The discovery of radium and polonium
Designing the first French steam railway
questions.explanation: Pasteur showed that microbes cause spoilage, which led to pasteurisation, and he developed a rabies vaccine in 1885. Radium and polonium were discovered by the Curies.

questions.stem: What did Louis Braille invent?
options: A reading system for blind people
A sign language for deaf people
questions.explanation: Louis Braille, blind from childhood, created a system of raised dots that is read by touch. Telegrams were sent in Morse code, an American invention.

questions.stem: Which French city is the centre of Airbus aircraft manufacturing?
questions.explanation: Airbus has its headquarters and main assembly lines at Toulouse, in the south-west. It is the standard example of European cooperation in manufacturing.

questions.stem: What was « le Minitel »?
options: A pre-internet online service on the phone line
The first French satellite launched from French Guiana
A small electric car built by a French carmaker
A French brand of mobile phone of the 2000s
questions.explanation: From the early 1980s, millions of French homes used Minitel terminals to look up directories, buy tickets and send messages. It closed in 2012, long after the internet had overtaken it.

questions.stem: What is « une avancée » in « une avancée majeure dans la recherche médicale »?
questions.explanation: « Une avancée » is a step forward, from « avancer ». A setback is « un revers » or « un recul ».

questions.stem: « Si l'intelligence artificielle facilite la vie, elle soulève aussi des questions éthiques. » What is the point?
options: AI has solved the ethical questions it once raised.
AI makes life easier but also raises ethical issues.
AI raises ethical questions only if it makes life easier.
AI makes life harder by raising ethical questions.
questions.explanation: Here « si » does not set a condition but concedes a point: 'while AI makes life easier…'. « Soulever des questions » means 'to raise questions'. Reading « si » as a strict 'if' is the trap.
